public_rationale: Italy had already imposed concrete obligations addressing inaccurate personal data generated by ChatGPT. That undermines a broad reading that accuracy-related legal duties did not exist. But the order allowed erasure when correction was technically infeasible and did not require solving general truthfulness or alignment. The UK evidence concerns one proposed framework. These records do not settle the contextual claim across the West, and the meaning of 'resolve' changes the result.

our_interpretation: The target is the law applicable on 25 April 2023, not legislation subsequently enacted.
The ordinary contextual reading concerns binding obligations to resolve the underlying reliability or alignment problems in AI systems.
A specific duty to correct or remove inaccurate personal data is relevant counterevidence, but is not automatically a duty to solve general truthfulness.
The West includes at least the United States, United Kingdom, and European Union. The phrase does not provide an exhaustive jurisdiction list.
criteria.support_condition: An adequately comprehensive legal review establishes that no Western jurisdiction imposed an applicable duty to resolve the general truthfulness or alignment problems identified in the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An identifiable law or binding order applicable on the post date required an AI company to resolve those general problems. A narrower remedial obligation contradicts only the broader reading that no legally enforceable accuracy-related duties existed.
